Three patient chart declarations call `createGlobalStore` directly, so they are the code that would be affected by a behaviour change in the framework:

1. **`openmrs-esm-patient-chart/packages/esm-patient-common-lib/src/store/patient-chart-store.ts`** (lines 19-25): creates the `patient-chart-global-store` store. Its hook `usePatientChartStore` (lines 55-71) and the setter `setPatientChartWorkspaceGroupVisitUuid` (lines 40-42) depend on it.
2. **`openmrs-esm-patient-chart/packages/esm-patient-common-lib/src/orders/store.ts`** (line 24): creates the `order-basket` store, which `_resetOrderBasketStore` (lines 29-31) also writes to.
3. **`openmrs-esm-patient-chart/packages/esm-form-entry-app/src/app/fe-wrapper/fe-wrapper.component.ts`** (line 35): creates the `ampath-form-state` store.

Code that reads or writes the two common-lib stores is also exposed to the change, though it calls the store rather than `createGlobalStore` itself. The order basket reads and writes are in `useOrderBasket.ts` and `postOrders.ts`. The `usePatientChartStore` callers are the largest group, and I listed the ones that the search surfaced.

`openmrs-esm-patient-chart/packages/esm-form-entry-app/src/openmrs-esm-framework.mock.ts` also defines a `createGlobalStore`, but it is a test mock and would not change with the real framework. I did not open it, so only its start line is cited.

The search covered the chart checkout only. Other openMRS products also call `createGlobalStore` (for example the dispensing app and the patient-management app), but they are outside the patient chart app.
